key_insight: Grasping-the-Future models future 3D hand and object motion together, including wrist movement, rather than treating them as separate prediction tasks. It learns from human interaction videos to anticipate how hands and objects could move next.
problem_solved: Learning to forecast coordinated hand-object interactions from internet videos requires recovering 3D motion from observed interactions and using it to predict plausible futures.
method: Use human videos of everyday activities as a source of hand-object interaction data.
Recover motion from completed interactions to support learning future motion.
Apply a unified generative model to jointly forecast 3D hand and object motion, including wrist movement.
impact: Joint forecasting could support more coordinated interaction prediction for robotics and other embodied AI systems. The supplied abstract is incomplete and provides no quantitative results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: internet video → recovered 3D motion → future interaction forecasts.
3D hand-and-object sequence with aligned wrist and object trajectories.
Timeline separating observed interaction frames from predicted future motion.
Branching future trajectories illustrating multiple plausible interaction outcomes.
paper_title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
paper_authors: Rustin Soraki, Matthew Wallingford, Ryan Aby, Brandon Chee, Jason Ren
